There the end of a transaction can delete an account that ran SELFDESTRUCT, and it is not proved here that the code of DAI never runs it (the library tracks instead that C is not created in the transaction and not marked for deletion, which EIP-6780 gives from Dencun).

contract_findings: SCOPE of this list: every item is read from the bytes and proved PER CALL (one successful call implies ...). No item is a theorem over a sequence of calls, and nothing here reads the live chain state (who holds a role today is not known to the proofs).

rely(usr) / deny(usr): only wards[caller] == 1; they write wards[usr] = 1 / 0. A ward can add or remove any ward, itself included. Both use the `note` modifier: one anonymous LOG4 with topics (selector shifted to the top 4 bytes, caller, first argument word, second argument word) and 288 bytes of data (the words 32 and 224, then the first 224 bytes of the call data, zeros past its end). The second argument word is read from the call data even though the functions have one argument. rely_readable and deny_readable state this log exactly.
mint(usr, wad): only wards[caller] == 1. A ward mints any amount to any address; the only checks are the overflow of balanceOf[usr] and of totalSupply. No cap, no zero-address check.
burn(usr, wad): no ward needed. The caller is usr, or has allowance[usr][caller] >= wad (an allowance of 2^256-1 is not reduced). balanceOf[usr] and totalSupply go down by wad.
transferFrom / move / pull / push: an allowance of 2^256-1 is not reduced; no zero-address checks.

permit: check order in the bytes: holder != 0, ecrecover == holder, expiry == 0 or now <= expiry, nonce == nonces[holder]; then the nonce write and allowance[holder][spender] = 0 or 2^256-1. The nonce increment is not checked for overflow (1 + old word, wrapping). The domain separator is the word of storage slot 5 (set at construction, not recomputed with CHAINID). v is masked to its low byte before the call.
After require(balance >= wad) and require(allowance >= wad) the code still runs the SafeMath sub check; it can never fail there (proved, rule sub_after_ge_lt).
Every function reverts on a nonzero value. name, symbol, version write nothing and log nothing.

transaction_theorems.file: DaiVerify/Dai/Tx.lean (171 lines, 10 theorems, 1 abbrev QMsg), on the shared library TokenKit/Seq (Frame, Run, Tx, Supply)
transaction_theorems.headline: supply_any_transactions: after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain) that EthLib's processTransaction runs, whoever sends them, whatever they call and however deep (calls back into DAI included), C still holds the code of DAI and the supply invariant Inv C holds, when both held on the block state before the first one. Every selector is included: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector.
transaction_theorems.supply_message_any_depth: one call run by EthLib's processMessage, to any account and any code, at any depth: 'C holds the code of DAI and the invariant holds' is kept, with or without an error. Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.Sane (a call that runs at C runs CODE), Seq.Good at the start, Seq.Clean of this run with Q := QMsg fork.
transaction_theorems.supply_transaction: one whole transaction run by EthLib's processTransaction (gas purchase, EIP-7702 authorizations, the message, call or creation, refunds, fee, deletion of accounts): block state before to block state after. Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam. Assumes Seq.TxClean of this transaction and Seq.Good at the start.
transaction_theorems.supply_any_transactions: the same after any finite list of transactions (Seq.Chain), each at its own fork (Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam) and in its own block environment.
transaction_theorems.supply_from_zero: the same from the base case shape: C holds the code and every storage word of C is zero (inv_zeroBase); conclusion Inv C after the list. This is NOT the real deployment state of DAI (the constructor run is not verified).
transaction_theorems.frameKeepsR: the per-frame premise of the library (Seq.FrameKeepsR: a frame that runs CODE at C under EthLib's real runner processRunner and ends with no error keeps Inv C), proved from the existing all-selector theorems: supply_permit (PermitSeq.lean) for permit, supply_preserved (Invariant.lean) for every other selector. Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam, any gas cap. No hypothesis on the runner is left: the STATICCALL to the ecrecover precompile is a message of the run like any other and the library induction covers it.
transaction_theorems.fork_range: transaction theorems: Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam for each transaction. Message theorem: Fork.paris <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam.
transaction_theorems.start_state: Seq.Good C CODE (Inv C) on the block state before the first transaction (assumed, see assumptions); supply_from_zero: Seq.HoldsCode plus all-zero storage of C.
transaction_theorems.older_model_kept: Seq.lean and PermitSeq.lean (inv_calls, inv_callsP, process_step, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, calls_process, callsP_process): top-level messages only, where every other step is ASSUMED to keep the storage of C (the constructor `other` with `Untouched`). This is the weaker per-message model. It is kept because other files and the axioms list use it; the theorems of Tx.lean do not use that assumption.

fork_range.headline: Every claim of this file is for Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam (transactions: Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam). Nothing is claimed for Glamsterdam or later.
fork_range.why: The proofs use the one-counter gas meter (Evm fork Nat). EthLib runs that meter only before Glamsterdam; from Glamsterdam it runs the two-counter meter of EIP-8037, which is not ported.
fork_range.stated_in_the_theorem: fork < .glamsterdam is a hypothesis of: ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, permitCall_process, callsP_process, frameKeepsR, supply_message_any_depth, supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero (Tx.lean), and of every theorem of Instance.lean and PermitRun.lean that is about a run (supply_m0, ecrecover_call_runs, permit_runs, supply_permit_m1, permit_runs_inv).
fork_range.not_stated_in_the_theorem: The older generated theorems (block rules, path specs, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, <fn>_readable, the Sanity witnesses) and the hand-written older per-message model of Seq.lean (process_step, process_step_inv, calls_process) carry only the lower bound (Berlin <= fork; Seq.lean from Paris). They are statements about the one-counter model and are true as stated at every such fork, but they describe what EthLib really runs only before Glamsterdam. The bound was NOT added to them: it would have to come from the generators in token-kit/scripts (shared by every token, outside the scope of this fix round), and adding a hypothesis that the proofs do not use would change no proof. Read each of them with fork < Glamsterdam; every headline that reaches a message or a transaction (the lists above) states it.

closed_instance.audit: the ten-token audit, fix 5 (DAI-3): PARTLY closed
closed_instance.plain_answer: There is NO closed instance of Sep, and so no theorem under Sep (supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit, the readable theorems of the writers, the sequence and transaction theorems) has an instance with every hypothesis proved. Each open fact of Sep says that a given slot is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a: a statement over 2^160 values of keccak. keccak is a real function here, but no proof can run it 2^160 times and no shorter argument is known (it is preimage and collision resistance). Under the usual random-function view each fact fails with chance about 2^-96.
closed_instance.state_and_call: state sState C []: one account at the contract C, every storage word 0. Call m0: allowance(K, K) sent by HOLDER, the address with the word K = 0x19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a (the address of the public test key 0x11...11), so the three mapping keys of the call are K, K, K.
proved_with_no_hypothesis: inv_start: the start invariant Inv holds in that state (sum of balances 0, total supply 0)
callKeys_m0, callKeys_m1: the keys of the two calls are [K, K, K]
computed by the kernel with the real keccak: allow_ne_total, nonce_ne_total, allow_ne_nonce, ward_ne_total
sep_iff, sep_m0_iff: Sep [K, K, K] holds exactly when KeyFacts holds (both directions), so the list of 5 facts below is the whole open part and cannot be made shorter
left_as_hypothesis: KeyFacts.total: slot 1 (the total supply) is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a
KeyFacts.uniq: no address word other than K has the balance slot of K
KeyFacts.allow: the allowance slot of (K, K) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.nonce: the nonce slot of K (mapping at slot 4) is the balance slot of no address word
KeyFacts.ward: the wards slot of K (mapping at slot 0) is the balance slot of no address word
closed_modulo_KeyFacts: supply_m0: every run of m0 from sState C [] that ends with no error ends in a state where Inv holds. Hypotheses: Berlin <= fork < Glamsterdam and KeyFacts; nothing else.

supply_permit_m1 (PermitRun.lean): the same for the permit call m1 under the real runner. Hypotheses: Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam and KeyFacts; nothing else (the start invariant, NoDelegation1, the size of the call data and the selector are discharged).
permit_runs_inv: the run of permit_runs exists and, under KeyFacts, ends in a state where Inv holds.
closed_instance.not_done: No base case was added to the sequence or transaction theorems beyond the existing supply_from_zero / inv_zeroBase (all-zero storage); inv_start is that base case for the concrete state. The real chain state is not used.

owner_facts.source: the ten-token audit, finding DAI-8: facts about the deployed bytes that the auditor confirmed and that matter to an owner or a user. Each is per call; none is a statement about live chain state.
facts: DAI-8.1: mint: the only checks are wards[caller] = 1 and no overflow of balanceOf[usr] and totalSupply; no cap, no zero address check. Any ward can make any address a ward; deny removes any ward, itself included. There is no theorem at sequence level about who the wards are or can become; that is live state.
DAI-8.2: burn: no ward needed; caller = usr, or allowance[usr][caller] >= wad (the largest word is not reduced).

DAI-8.3: permit: the digest uses the word of storage slot 5 as domain separator; the bytes have no CHAINID opcode, so the separator is fixed at construction and a signature is valid on any chain fork that shares this storage. The allowance is set to 0 or to the largest word only. expiry = 0 means no expiry. The nonce sum is unchecked. v is cut to its low byte. Only ECRECOVER is used: a contract holder cannot permit.
DAI-8.4: transferFrom, pull, move, burn skip the allowance when caller = src and never reduce an allowance equal to the largest word.
DAI-8.5: every function reverts on value; a nonzero value at top level is proved to fail (process_value_fails).
DAI-8: the readable theorems give necessary conditions and exact effects of a successful call; that a call CAN succeed is shown only by the witnesses.
